qualifications: Response says coda and package diagnostics may differ but does not explain known autoburnin window difference. ESS uses all 20 kept draws per chain while this coda Rhat uses only 10. Sampler burn-in is distinct from the extra automatic diagnostic trimming.

High ESS implies improved numerical precision relative to posterior variation under valid target sampling; absolute Monte Carlo error also depends on variance, so high ESS alone does not establish a small absolute error.
Trapped-in-a-mode example can illustrate misleading ESS; a literally constant chain does not provide a useful high ESS. Wording stuck in one location is imprecise if interpreted literally.
More iterations can improve ESS after valid mixing but do not by themselves guarantee resolution of a large Rhat or multimodality.
